stream: SINP International Skilled Worker: Occupations In-Demand

officialProgramPage.label: Saskatchewan: International Skilled Worker – Occupations In-Demand

steps.title: Check Occupations In-Demand eligibility
steps.description: Confirm you have at least 60 SINP points, at least CLB 4, related post-secondary education and skilled work experience, an eligible in-demand occupation, settlement funds and a genuine intention to live in Saskatchewan. This route does not require a Saskatchewan job offer or an Express Entry profile.

requiredDocuments.title: SINP point assessment showing at least 60 points

officialLinks.label: Saskatchewan: International Skilled Worker – Occupations In-Demand

preparationChecklist.text: Confirm you live outside Canada or have proof of legal status in Canada.
Check the current occupation restrictions and any professional-status or licensing requirements.
Confirm you genuinely intend to live and work in Saskatchewan.

officialLinks.label: Saskatchewan: International Skilled Worker – Occupations In-Demand

commonMistakes: Using criteria from another SINP category.
Assuming 60 points guarantees an invitation or nomination.
Ignoring occupation-specific licensing or exclusion rules.

steps.title: Complete language, education and occupation preparation
steps.description: Obtain a valid approved language result meeting at least CLB 4, and obtain an ECA for education completed outside Canada. Check whether Saskatchewan requires professional status or licensing evidence for the intended occupation.

preparationChecklist.text: Confirm every language ability meets the applicable minimum.
Confirm the education or training relates to the intended occupation.
Start any required licensing or professional-status process early.

officialLinks.label: Saskatchewan: International Skilled Worker – Occupations In-Demand

commonMistakes: Using an expired language result or ECA.
Claiming education or work that does not relate to the intended occupation.
Waiting until invitation to investigate a required licence.

steps.title: Prepare evidence for the SINP points and settlement requirements
steps.description: Collect proof for every point you plan to claim, including employment references, education, language, age and Saskatchewan connections. Prepare the required settlement plan and maintain qualifying settlement funds for the required period.

requiredDocuments.title: Detailed employer reference letters for claimed work experience

requiredDocuments.title: Evidence of claimed Saskatchewan connections
requiredDocuments.condition: Required for any Saskatchewan connection or adaptability points claimed.

officialLinks.label: Saskatchewan: International Skilled Worker – Occupations In-Demand

preparationChecklist.text: Calculate the SINP score conservatively and retain evidence for every claim.
Check the current family-size amount and required fund-history rules.
Ensure employment letters describe dates, hours, duties and employer contact information.

officialLinks.label: Saskatchewan: International Skilled Worker – Occupations In-Demand

commonMistakes: Claiming points without documents that prove them.
Moving borrowed funds into an account shortly before applying.
Using employment letters that omit duties, hours or dates.

steps.title: Submit an International Skilled Worker EOI
steps.description: Create one accurate EOI profile for this category. An EOI is not a provincial application; it enters the candidate into a ranked pool, remains valid for one year and does not guarantee an invitation.

requiredDocuments.title: Accurate passport, occupation, ECA, licensing and points information

officialLinks.label: Saskatchewan: International Skilled Worker EOI system

preparationChecklist.text: Choose Occupations In-Demand; Saskatchewan does not allow simultaneous EOIs in both categories.
Verify every answer and point claim before submission.
Save the EOI confirmation and profile details.

officialLinks.label: Saskatchewan: International Skilled Worker EOI system

commonMistakes: Treating the EOI as a complete SINP application.
Maintaining more than one active International Skilled Worker EOI.
Inflating the score or omitting material information.

steps.title: Keep the EOI current and wait for an invitation
steps.description: Monitor the EOI and Saskatchewan notices. Candidates are selected according to score, labour-market needs, occupation and annual allocation. Saskatchewan currently publishes no scheduled EOI draws, so timing and selection are uncertain.

preparationChecklist.text: Monitor email, OASIS and official SINP notices.
If information changes, follow Saskatchewan's instructions to cancel and resubmit the EOI.
Track the one-year EOI validity period and document expiry dates.

officialLinks.label: Saskatchewan: International Skilled Worker EOI system

commonMistakes: Assuming an EOI creates a right to be invited.
Letting the EOI or supporting documents expire.
Failing to correct a changed score, occupation or family circumstance.

steps.title: Prepare the SINP application after invitation
steps.description: If invited, use the same OASIS account and prepare the complete provincial application within the 60-day deadline. Every EOI claim must be supported, and missing or untranslated documents can cause the application to be closed.

steps.title: Submit and pay for the SINP application
steps.description: Complete all OASIS sections, upload the complete evidence package, pay the non-refundable $500 application fee through the official process and submit before the invitation expires.

requiredDocuments.title: Complete OASIS application and supporting documents

officialLinks.label: Saskatchewan: International Skilled Worker procedures
Saskatchewan: International Skilled Worker – Occupations In-Demand

preparationChecklist.text: Review all answers, uploads and declarations.
Submit before the invitation deadline rather than waiting until the final day.
Save the application number, payment receipt and submission confirmation.

officialLinks.label: Saskatchewan: International Skilled Worker – Occupations In-Demand
Saskatchewan: International Skilled Worker procedures

commonMistakes: Paying through an unofficial site or representative account.
Submitting an incomplete package because a document has been requested but not received.
Keeping another active SINP application at the same time.

steps.title: Wait for SINP assessment and respond to requests
steps.description: SINP first checks completeness and then assesses eligibility, points, documents and intention to reside in Saskatchewan. Monitor all communications, respond by each deadline and report material changes.

preparationChecklist.text: Monitor OASIS and email for requests or a decision.
Respond completely within every stated deadline.
Report changes to family, address, status, occupation or Express Entry information when applicable.

officialLinks.label: Saskatchewan: International Skilled Worker procedures
Saskatchewan: SINP processing statistics

governmentTimeline.description: SINP states a service goal of processing complete International Skilled Worker applications within 16 weeks. This is a goal, not a prediction or guarantee.
governmentTimeline.scope: Provincial processing after SINP receives a complete application

commonMistakes: Ignoring a request because the original package appeared complete.
Failing to report a material change.
Treating the 16-week service goal as a guaranteed decision date.

steps.title: Review the nomination and prepare the federal application
steps.description: If Saskatchewan nominates you, review the nomination package, its expiry date and conditions. Prepare the current non-Express Entry Provincial Nominee Program forms and supporting documents for the federal application.

officialLinks.label: IRCC: Non-Express Entry PNP documents

requiredDocuments.title: Current federal PNP forms and document checklist

officialLinks.label: IRCC: Non-Express Entry PNP documents

preparationChecklist.text: Record the nomination expiry date and conditions.
Use the current federal online forms and checklist.
Prepare police certificates and civil records as instructed.

officialLinks.label: Saskatchewan: International Skilled Worker – Occupations In-Demand
IRCC: Non-Express Entry PNP documents

commonMistakes: Using Express Entry instructions for a non-Express Entry nomination.
Waiting until the nomination is close to expiry to prepare the federal application.

steps.title: Submit the non-Express Entry permanent residence application
steps.description: Apply online through the federal Permanent Residence Portal, upload the nomination confirmation and required documents, pay the applicable federal fees and submit before the nomination expires.

officialLinks.label: IRCC: Apply for PR through the non-Express Entry PNP
IRCC: Apply for PR through the non-Express Entry PNP

preparationChecklist.text: Check that every form, signature, upload and fee is complete.
Submit while the Saskatchewan nomination remains valid.
Save the submission confirmation and acknowledgement of receipt.

officialLinks.label: IRCC: Apply for PR through the non-Express Entry PNP
IRCC: Non-Express Entry PNP documents

commonMistakes: Submitting through the Express Entry account instead of the PR Portal.
Omitting the nomination confirmation or fee receipt.
Submitting an incomplete application that IRCC returns.

steps.title: Complete federal medical, biometrics and document requests
steps.description: Follow IRCC instructions for biometrics, medical examinations, police certificates, interviews or additional documents. A provincial nomination does not by itself authorize work in Canada, so maintain lawful status separately when applicable.

preparationChecklist.text: Monitor the PR Portal and IRCC communications.
Complete biometrics within the deadline in the instruction letter when required.
Maintain lawful temporary status and work authorization when applicable.

officialLinks.label: IRCC: After applying through the non-Express Entry PNP

commonMistakes: Assuming nomination automatically extends immigration status or work authorization.
Completing biometrics or medical steps without following IRCC instructions.

steps.title: Receive the federal permanent residence decision
steps.description: IRCC assesses admissibility and makes the final permanent residence decision. If approved, follow the confirmation and landing instructions and continue intending to settle in Saskatchewan.

preparationChecklist.text: Read and follow the IRCC decision instructions.
Complete the permanent residence confirmation process.
Keep the nomination and federal records.

officialLinks.label: IRCC: After applying through the non-Express Entry PNP

commonMistakes: Treating provincial approval as final federal approval.
Making irreversible decisions before permanent residence is granted.
